scenes.title: Where and when
narration: In 1952, American music presenter John Coast sought to bring a Balinese dance troupe to Europe and the United States.
He approached master choreographer I Ketut Marya (I Mario) of Tabanan, Bali, who had previously created the kebyar duduk dance in 1925.
Working alongside Coast, dancer I Wayan Sampih, and local musicians, I Mario drew upon images of Western ballet to craft a fusion dance.
on_screen: Map: Indonesia · Southeast Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Oleg is a balih-balihan (secular entertainment) dance.
Beyond its romantic plot, writer Kartika Suardana notes the garden symbolism conveys that both sexes naturally need each other.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: GunungSari | PuriAgungPliatan | OLEG TAMULILINGAN (https://archive.org/details/20150822GunungSariPuriPliatanOlegTamulilinganDayuAloHD720p)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance dramatises a garden encounter between two bumblebees.
The female dancer enters first, executing complex, agile movements to depict fluttering around flowers and gathering nectar.
The male dancer enters with a fan and pursues her with insistent flirtation.
Watch for Wing Flight Scarf Motion, Fan Pursuit.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (RUCbV8C9CVE)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Duet dynamic; male dancer pursues female dancer across an open performance floor

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The female dancer wears traditional prada fabric embellished with gold paint, a long sheer scarf serving as bee wings, and a large bouquet of flowers on her head.
The male dancer wears prada fabric wrapped to trail behind him like a tail, an udeng headpiece, and carries a fan throughout the performance.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Choreographer I Ketut Marya (I Mario); presenter John Coast; original dancers I Gusti Rasmin Raka, I Wayan Sampih (1926–1954), and Raka Rasmi; ethnomusicologist Andrew McGraw.
Originating in Tabanan, Oleg is performed throughout Bali.
Evolved from 1920s gamelan gong kebyar dance developments (kebyar duduk) and 1950s cross-cultural dialogue between Balinese masters and Western presenters.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Oleg is parent of Kebyar duduk: Also choreographed by I Ketut Marya (I Mario) in 1925, establishing the kebyar dance style.
Oleg is sibling of Cendrawasih: Shares the Balinese genre of animal-themed theatrical dances.
Oleg is influence of Legong: Young Balinese dancers often trained in legong before learning oleg.
